images.seen: A Karoo stone cottage at frosty golden dawn, chimney smoke rising dead straight, two steaming enamel mugs standing on the frosted stone wall. Saturday.
lines: Smoke going straight up means cold, still and not one breath of wind.
Frost on the wall, steam on the mugs: the morning is minus-something and perfect.
The chimney got lit before the kettle did, and both were the right call.

images.seen: A man walking to work with his roll-neck jersey pulled up over his nose, satchel on his shoulder, wet paving and a bare tree under a grey sky. Friday.
lines: The jersey got promoted to balaclava somewhere between the door and the gate.
The air found the one gap in the outfit and he is closing it by hand.
Ja, it's jersey weather. Double jersey.

images.seen: An elderly man under a knitted blanket in an armchair pulled up to a glowing bar heater, tea on the side table, bare branches and grey through the window. Sunday.
lines: Chair turned to the heater, blanket up, tea close: winter Sunday, executed correctly.
Every bar of that heater is on, which is all the weather report you need.
Cold enough that the armchair migrated toward the plug points.

images.seen: A garden tap furred completely white with frost, one drop hanging from the spout, frosted herbs and a brick house behind, pale clear sky. Monday.
lines: The garden tap grew a white beard overnight; the night was that serious.
That drop has been thinking about letting go since about four this morning.
Frost right down to the washers — last night went properly below zero.
